subject: Payment staging, invoice split & tax ownership for Redwood order
messages:
From: BrightBridge Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@brightbridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: Invoicing cadence + tax residency questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. Procurement has a few items to close before we can route a PO:

- We generally require one PO per legal entity (we have US Ops LLC and EU Services Ltd). Can Redwood split invoicing so each entity is billed for its consumption?
- For tax/VAT handling: who will be responsible for VAT on the EU invoices? We need a statement of tax liability and a copy of Redwood's VAT ID or W-9 for our finance team.
- On minimum commit: procurement prefers a staggered commit across quarters rather than a single upfront spend. Do you support amortized billing or multiple invoices tied to milestones?
- Net terms: BrightBridge standard is Net 45 for first-year vendor relationships unless otherwise approved. Would Redwood accept Net 45?

Attached our PO template (BB_PO_Template.pdf) for reference. Please confirm and share a draft Order Form we can submit to legal.

Thanks,
Sam Ortega
Head of Procurement, BrightBridge Analytics
procurement@brightbridge.com

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: BrightBridge Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-09T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Invoicing cadence + tax residency questions

Hi Sam — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. I looped in Laura (sales ops) and Karthik (contracts) so we can align internal approvals. Quick answers and next steps below:

- Invoice split across entities: we can issue separate invoices if you provide the billing legal entity names and PO numbers for each entity. Redwood will need to map the billed usage to the billing entity; we typically split usage by project tags or by seat allocation. If you want us to issue multiple invoices for the same subscription, we can, but we need an explicit split table on the Order Form.

- Tax/VAT responsibility: Redwood typically charges VAT where we are required by local tax rules. We can accept customer-responsible VAT handling (i.e., customer self-accounting) provided BrightBridge confirms the tax treatment in writing and supplies the applicable VAT IDs. Please send the VAT IDs or W-9 for each entity.

- Minimum commit / amortization: we can structure the commit to amortize across quarters or months. I'll attach a draft Order Form with two options (upfront commit amortized monthly OR quarterly staged commit). See Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx (attached).

- Net terms: We can accept Net 45 for the first contract year. For future renewals we typically move to Net 30. If procurement requires Net 45 permanently, that will affect pricing by ~1.0% to cover financing — let us know if that's acceptable.

Next actions: please confirm the exact legal entity names and PO numbers, and whether you want the commit amortized monthly or in quarterly tranches. Once we have that, Karthik will produce a redlined Order Form for your legal.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-10T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: internal: recommended invoice split and commit cadence for BrightBridge

Vivek / team — thinking through BrightBridge's ask: recommended approach to minimize back-and-forth with procurement/legal:

Proposal A (preferred):
- Split invoices by legal entity. BrightBridge provides two PO numbers mapped to US Ops LLC (US) and EU Services Ltd (EU).
- Put an "Invoice Allocation" annex in the Order Form showing exact percentage or USD allocation per quarter. That makes accounting straightforward and avoids re-allocations.

Proposal B (if PO constraints):
- Single master invoice issued to parent with internal allocation note. Finance will accept this only if BrightBridge signs an allocation confirmation.

Minimum commit: suggest an amortized quarterly schedule: Q1 30%, Q2 25%, Q3 25%, Q4 20% — ties to expected ramp and reduces initial cash friction.

Net terms: Marcus — we can accept Net 45 for year one. Do you want a pricing uplift to cover the extended terms? If so, +1.0% is our standard.

Attaching an invoice split example to show how we'd present multi-entity billing in our invoices: invoice-split-examples.xlsx

Laura
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: internal: recommended invoice split and commit cadence for BrightBridge

Thanks — finance reviewed. A few points for the Order Form redline and SOW language:

1) Net terms: we approve Net 45 for year one with the +1.0% pricing uplift baked into the payment schedule. Please confirm whether BrightBridge will accept the uplift; if not, finance will require a prepayment (partial upfront) to mitigate credit exposure.

2) Invoice allocation: we need the Order Form to include an "Invoice Allocation" table (three columns: billing entity, PO number, allocation %) and a sentence: "Customer certifies that the allocation above is final; any subsequent reallocation requires mutual written agreement."

3) Tax evidence: for EU billing we must collect VAT ID and a certificate of tax residency if BrightBridge wishes to shift VAT liability. Add a clause: "Customer shall provide VAT IDs and any required tax residency evidence within 10 business days of Order Form execution." We will not process EU invoices without the VAT ID.

4) Attachments: please include the final signed PO as an attachment reference in the Order Form so procurement's PO number is cross-referenced on our invoice.

I'll prepare the exact clause language and send it to Karthik for insertion.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.inference
Attachment: TaxResidency_Evidence.pdf (sample)

---
From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@brightbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: BrightBridge Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Invoicing cadence + tax residency questions

Vivek — thanks, this is very helpful. BrightBridge confirms the following and is ready to proceed:

- Legal entities and POs: US Ops LLC — PO #BB-US-778; EU Services Ltd — PO #BB-EU-779.
- VAT handling: BrightBridge will accept customer self-accounting for VAT on EU invoices. We'll provide the VAT IDs and tax residency cert within 5 business days.
- Commit cadence: we accept the amortized quarterly schedule you proposed (30%/25%/25%/20%).
- Net terms: we accept Net 45 for year one. The +1.0% uplift is acceptable.

Attached is a signed PO referencing the two entity PO numbers (Signed_PO_BrightBridge.pdf). Please share the redlined Order Form with the Invoice Allocation annex and tax clause, and we will get that to legal for signature.

Sam Ortega
Head of Procurement, BrightBridge Analytics
procurement@brightbridge.com
Attachment: Signed_PO_BrightBridge.pdf
